title: Troubled life of shooting victim Daniel Lamer
article: Nov. 1982: Tried and convicted in adult court for kidnapping and other offences. Sentenced to 18 years in prison.
1982: Escapes from an armoured car during a transfer. Armed with a shotgun, he wounds one guard before being recaptured and re- incarcerated.
1984: Closely watched as guards suspect he is preparing to escape.
April 12, 1991: Police issue an arrest warrant after parole conditions are broken.

May 6-7, 1991: With accomplice Alain Beaupre, robs a Jean Coutu pharmacy in Montreal for $68. During the escape, they kidnap a Montreal police officer and another man and hold them hostage in an apartment for 16 hours. The standoff ends in a bloody gunfight between the officer and his kidnappers. All four men are shot before he and Mr. Beaupre surrender. A new sentence of 22 years is tacked onto the nine leftover from his previous sentence. He is ordered to serve the time in Donnacona Institution.
1991: Placed in solitary confinement after guards find a handmade ladder.
1992: While being transferred back to jail, escapes from an armoured car. He is captured an hour and a half later.
1992: Asks to be moved to another jail to 'start over.' The request is approved.
1992-1997: Takes high school courses and is awarded a diploma. Also takes technical courses to try to increase his employability.
July 1997: Suspected of being the assistant to the head of a prison drug ring. The charge is never proven.
1998: Starts work as a mechanic, part of a part-time, non-paid work placement. This is followed by a full-time placement.
Jan. 26, 1999: Allowed unescorted visits to his common-law wife's house for 48 hours per month for the first four months, 72 hours per month thereafter.
Nov. 30,1999: petitions for conditional parole and day parole are refused. Request to extend program of unescorted visits is granted.
March 22, 2000: After breaking up with his wife, is allowed to visit his parents on unescorted trips. A brother who served time, and a sister, live at the same address.
March 2000: Starts paid work as a mechanic.
March 11, 2002: During a routine traffic stop, opens fire on OPP officers, hitting Const. Dan Brisson in the back. Officers return fire, hitting him three times and killing him.
